editorial.headline: Organising a Tourism District
editorial.standfirst: This activity organises the land, development units and administration of a tourism area, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Tourism-area management begins with land, but its remit is the organisation of an entire tourism precinct. The activity covers laying out and further dividing land into defined nodes or neighbourhoods; building or leasing those units for businesses that will develop the tourism facilities and infrastructure the area requires. It also includes carrying out and/or supervising tourism-business development under the existing requirements, and building or providing space for business administration within the area. It is an area-wide role.

The code is available to medium and large enterprises. That scale setting fits the work described: it is an operating mandate for a managed tourism area, rather than a single facility inside one. A registrant may be responsible for arranging the land, making development units available, overseeing the tourism development that follows, and ensuring that administration has a place within the managed area. The individual units can be built or leased, but their purpose is fixed: to accommodate businesses developing the tourism support required in the district. The activity also keeps the administrative needs of those businesses within the perimeter of the managed area.

Nationally, the PMA position is open and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. Put plainly, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity; it does not set a lower foreign-equity ceiling. The stated national PMA source underpins that position. For a founder assessing the activity on its own terms, that is the starting position: PMA is open nationally, at the stated 100% ceiling. It is an activity-specific national position, not a general conclusion about tourism investment.

Bali changes neither that national ownership figure nor the basic registration conclusion recorded here. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for activities assessed at Low or Medium-Low risk. At the large-enterprise scale for this activity, however, the OSS risk is Medium-High or High. The record therefore says it is not blocked by the moratorium and gives its Bali status as OK or Higher Risk. The honest local reading is straightforward: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today; the Bali result is not a hidden closure, but a route outside the moratorium’s Low and Medium-Low risk block.
